questions.question: Q1 As the sputtering cycle proceeds over time, why does the digital ohmmeter display a drop in resistance?

answers.a: The length of the trace is actively shrinking
answers.b: The metal layer is building up, widening the conductive path area
answers.c: The system temperature is dropping below absolute freezing points
answers.d: The choice of metal is swapping automatically to lower values

explanations.a: Track channel length bounds remain fixed by the substrate trench mask layout.
explanations.b: Correct! As metal fills the trench, cross section thickness scales up, cutting resistance.
explanations.c: Chamber cooling loops maintain uniform thermal boundaries, not extreme drops.
explanations.d: The source material targets cannot swap elements mid-deposition process.

questions.question: Q2 If you select Copper instead of Aluminum or Tungsten, what happens to the output diagnostics?

answers.a: The net resistance drops due to Copper's lower bulk resistivity profile
answers.b: The trace line becomes physically longer inside the center chamber view
answers.c: The line stops conducting current completely
answers.d: The thickness slider value is locked to a fixed minimum boundary

explanations.a: Correct! Copper possesses low natural resistivity, optimizing track conductivity.
explanations.b: Material modifications don't change geometric channel length footprints.
explanations.c: Copper is an excellent electronic conductor widely used across advanced computing platforms.
explanations.d: Slider input boundaries operate independently of chemical metal choices.

questions.question: Q3 Shrinking both Wire Width and Wire Thickness simultaneously results in:

answers.a: An exponential spike in line resistance
answers.b: A complete drop in bulk material conductivity values
answers.c: A higher processing quality score rating from electro-migration metrics
answers.d: The visual track expanding to cover the active silicon label layer

explanations.a: Correct! Compressing both dimensions creates a severe geometric electron bottleneck.
explanations.b: Conductivity is an inherent material property and does not scale with dimension changes.
explanations.c: Severely downscaling wires increases current congestion, lowering device reliability.
explanations.d: Lowering values shrinks the graphics profiles inside your viewport modules.

questions.question: Q4 What physical phenomenon causes the dislodgement of target atoms inside the simulation chamber?

answers.a: Chemical acid dissolution along photoresist profiles
answers.b: Kinetic energy transfer via high-speed plasma ion collisions
answers.c: Thermal evaporation caused by structural laser melting heaters
answers.d: High-voltage magnetic mass analyzer filter sweeps

explanations.a: Chemical dissolution handles liquid wet etching profile steps.
explanations.b: Correct! Sputtering relies on gas plasma ions smashing atoms out of target faces.
explanations.c: Thermal evaporation is a separate PVD technique that uses resistive heating, not plasma.
explanations.d: Mass analyzers handle ion species tracking, not physical target abrasion loops.

questions.question: Q5 What defect risk lowers the 'Connection Quality' score when width is dialed to extremely low thresholds?

explanations.a: Amorphization tracks deep silicon lattice damage caused by ion beam collisions.
explanations.b: Correct! High electron currents in tiny wires physically push metal atoms out of place.
explanations.c: Under-etching relates to faulty pattern development phases before metallization.
explanations.d: Outgassing covers vacuum vapor release risks from unbaked processing plastics.

questions.question: Q6 Why do white arrow patterns appear flowing through the metal wire path during Step 5?

answers.a: To illustrate gas plasma venting out of extraction ports
answers.b: To signify active electron current flowing across the complete circuit track
answers.c: To track photoresist masks being stripped cleanly off trenches
answers.d: To indicate structural cracks forming inside the silicon oxide base

explanations.a: Plasma loops are sealed during active operation cycles, not vented across substrates.
explanations.b: Correct! Flow particles show that the track is solid and conducting electric current.
explanations.c: Stripping runs as an independent chemical cleaning stage outside PVD tool suites.
explanations.d: Flow loops track operating electron current pathways, not fracture defects.

questions.question: Q7 Which material provides high reliability and is preferred for vertical contact plugs?

explanations.a: Aluminum handles general interconnect wiring but lacks high thermal resistance.
explanations.b: Correct! Tungsten's high melting point makes it ideal for local transistor contact plugs.
explanations.c: Copper handles horizontal multi-level wiring highways but requires barrier layers.
explanations.d: Silicon Dioxide serves as the insulating barrier layer around the metal plug.

questions.question: Q8 How does cross-sectional area (A) mathematically relate to line resistance (R)?

answers.a: Resistance is directly proportional to cross-sectional area
answers.b: Resistance is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area
answers.c: Resistance is completely independent of wire area scaling metrics
answers.d: Resistance matches area parameters multiplied by target lengths squared

explanations.a: If they were directly proportional, larger areas would increase resistance.
explanations.b: Correct! Area is in the denominator, meaning a larger area lowers line resistance.
explanations.c: Cross section dimensions directly control net structural carrier channel bottlenecks.
explanations.d: The math models straight inverse fractions, skipping exponential lengths terms.

questions.question: Q9 In the separated cross-section monitor view, what layer serves as the structural 'mold' walls?

answers.b: The Bulk Silicon base floor layer
answers.d: The pure metal target block face

explanations.a: Correct! Pre-etched oxide trenches act as insulating side walls for the wire track.
explanations.b: The silicon floor supports the transistors beneath the wire paths.
explanations.c: Vacuum boundaries define space dimensions, not sub-micron wafer features.
explanations.d: The target block sits above the wafer as the source of metal atoms.

questions.question: Q10 What is a core process advantage of multi-level metallization stacking?

answers.a: It allows complex routing configurations across multiple independent vertical layers
answers.b: It eliminates the need to use pure metal materials like Copper
answers.c: It forces resistance metrics to drop back into absolute zero ranges natively
answers.d: It removes vacuum constraints from the sputtering chamber tools completely

explanations.a: Correct! Stacking lets fabs build 10-15 layers of wires vertically to maximize space.
explanations.b: Material purity remains crucial for every vertical layer to ensure proper function.
explanations.c: Dropping resistance to zero requires superconductive cooling steps, not layer stacking.
explanations.d: Every vertical metallization track requires vacuum processing to avoid contamination.
